item.title: Davis Makerspace & Clothing Repair Cafe — Tue Sep 1, 6:00 PM — Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch Library
item.description:
Davis Makerspace is a community workspace for makers and builders, designers and inventors. A small assortment of tools will be available for use and staff or volunteers will be on hand to provide some assistance. Supervised children are welcome. Participants must provide a signed liability waiver (available on site). Mondays & Tuesdays, 6p—8p; Thursdays, 9:30a—11:30a.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Live Jazz: Jim Frink Trio — Tue Sep 1, 7:30 PM — Root of Happiness Kava Bar
item.description:
Jim Frink is an active drummer and educator based in Davis. The jazz trio plays improvisational music, ranging from standards, to modern jazz, to balkan folk and beyond. This event takes place every 1st and 3rd Tuesday of the month – 7:30-10:30pm
Source: The Dirt

item.title: UpENDing Parkinson's at Rocknasium — Wed Sep 2, 10:00 AM — Rocknasium the Climbing Gym
item.description:
UpENDing Parkinson’s at Rocknasium Wednesdays, 10-11:30 AM Rocknasium is hosting UpENDing Parkinson’s, a non-profit that provides guided rock climbing to those living with Parkinson’s. Entrance is free, and rental gear is $10. Those interested may register as a climber here.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Genealogy Club Library Hours — Wed Sep 2, 1:00 PM — Davis Senior Center
item.description:
Library Hours: Wednesdays, 1 – 3:30 p.m. (excluding holidays) This group assists and maintains the Senior Center’s extensive Genealogy Library, and in addition, hosts monthly lectures and meetings. During library hours, members are available to assist you with accessing research materials. Computer access is also available in the library for research purposes.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The Bike Garage Open Hours: Davis Location — Wed Sep 2, 1:00 PM — Bike Garage Davis
item.description:
Davis location: 606 Peña Drive #300
FREE Bike Repair
Come to the Bike Garage, where our volunteer mechanics will repair your bike. We accept cash, Venmo, and Paypal donations. Interested in becoming a volunteer bike mechanic? No experience is necessary.
CONTACT US TO VOLUNTEER
Quality Used Bikes for SaleLowest prices on the best used bikes.Our inventory changes every day!
Hybrid bikes, town bikes, vintage bikes, road bikes, mountain bikes, kids’ bikes, and more. Visit the Bike Garage in Davis or Woodland to check out our inventory.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Bird Photography by Maya Mehta — Wed Sep 2, 3:00 PM — Super Owl Brewing
item.description:
Maya Mehta, an 8th grader in Davis, will be showing her bird photography at Super Owl Brewing in September. Maya started her birding and photography journey during the pandemic, when she was 7. Encouraged by her parents with an old camera, she has been sharing her pictures from India and the US regularly at local venues. This will be her 4th year sharing her pictures at Super Owl.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Sep 2, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Pub Quiz (Trivia) hosted by Dr. Andy — Wed Sep 2, 7:00 PM — Sudwerk Brewing Co.
item.description:
Sudwerk Trivia is a free, first come-first serve, all-ages event. Join us for a fun-filled evening of brain-teasing questions and friendly competition at Sudwerk’s Pub Quiz every Wednesday from 7-9pm! Put your knowledge to the test and gather your friends for a night of laughter and excitement. Location: 2001 2nd Street, Davis, CA 95618 You do not have to be 21+ to participate in trivia. There is no drink minimum.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:
Join Ms. Sue for Mother Goose on the Loose!
Mother Goose on the Loose is an award-winning early literacy program for toddlers (ages 2-3) and their grown-ups. It combines music, movement, rhymes, and books to help young children develop language skills, social and emotional skills, general knowledge about the world, and a love of learning.
Every Tuesday in the Blanchard Room of the Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch Library.

item.title: Davis Farmers Market - Every Saturday from 8am - 1pm — Sat Nov 7, 12:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Experience the heart and soul of Davis every Saturday at the Davis Farmers Market in Central Park! 🗓 Every Saturday⏰ 8:00 AM – 1:00 PM📍 Central Park, Davis Shop fresh from the source with local farmers and vendors offering: 🥕 Fresh, seasonal produce🌻 Farm products🛍 Handmade crafts🥖 Fresh-baked goods☕ Coffee and hot food Whether you’re stocking up on locally grown ingredients, enjoying breakfast in the park, or simply soaking in the vibrant community atmosphere, the Davis Farmers Market is a beloved weekly tradition for all ages. Bring your family, support local growers and makers, and enjoy the bounty of our fertile region every Saturday!
Source: Davis Downtown

item.title: The Davis Bookworms — Sun Aug 30, 1:30 PM — Nashoba Wines
item.description:
Do you want to make time for reading? Join The Davis Bookworms! Bring whatever book you’re reading or want to read. We read together for an hour and then discuss what we read for about an hour. After that, the conversation goes in whatever direction it wants to go. Every other Sunday.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: August Open Mic & Music Trivia — Sun Aug 30, 6:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Whether you’re looking for a venue to share your own talents or just looking to enjoy hearing (and seeing) some local performers, we invite you to this free monthly event. We provide the sound, stage and lights – the rest is up to you. Play us your favorite song, tell us some jokes, act out a scene from your favorite play with friends. We will continue to feature our Music Trivia contest throughout the evening in between acts. The winner will receive a $20 Watermelon Music gift card! We ask that each performance be suitable for an all-ages venue, and that you arrive on time and stay until the end to support your fellow performers. FREE!!! Doors open/sign-ups @ 5:30. First act @ 6:00. Please help support the Watermelon Music with your purchase of a drink or a snack at Open Mic! Non-alcoholic drinks and pre-packaged snacks are available for sale at The Melon Ball. (Cash or Venmo only) We hope to see you there!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: International Folk Dancing — Sun Aug 30, 7:00 PM — Davis Community Church
item.description:
Connect with other cultures, while connecting to other people Sunday nights 7p-9:30p first time free all levels welcome Community Church Fireside Room at 412 C Street, Davis (Fireside Room. Entrance on C-St. near 4th.)
Visit http://davisfolkdancers.org/ to check for our current meeting location, which changes periodically.

item.title: Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz — Tue Sep 1, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz Tuesdays, 10 AM – 12 PM | September 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 $170 Members, $190 Non-Members (Materials not included) This 5-week workshop with Misuk Goltz will focus on using your brushes to their full potential and practicing diverse hand motions to achieve painterly, expressive watercolor paintings. Students will learn how to distribute different values to create balanced and sophisticated artwork while painting various subjects. Please note that this class is intended for participants who have previous experience with watercolor techniques and color blending. The use of high-quality watercolor materials is strongly recommended to achieve the best results. Register here: https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/ Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Coloring Book Club — Tue Sep 1, 5:30 PM — the Atelier
item.description:
Unwind with the Charmed coloring book by local artist Karen Sue Chen. This 4-week series offers a dedicated space for coloring, socializing, and lowering cortisol levels through meditative focus. Includes the featured book; media available as an add-on. What is the Atelier? Located in Midtown Sacramento, The Atelier is a contemporary studio and gallery dedicated to empowering creators of all ages.

item.title: Disappeared in America Visibility Event - Woodland (1st Wednesday) — Wed Sep 2, 4:30 PM — In front of the new courthouse
item.description:
In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison. Disappeared in America is a Yolo County day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 🚨 On the 1st Wednesday of the month, we’re showing up in Woodland in front of the new courthouse at 1000 Main St.

item.title: Free Yoga Practice — Thu Sep 17, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community 🌀 **Move with intention. Connect with your body. Celebrate community.**
Join us every **Thursday at 6 PM** for an embodied yoga practice designed to help you release tension, ground yourself, and cultivate presence. This is a trauma-informed, all-levels class, no prior yoga experience needed. Expect a Hatha-Vinyasa flow, breathwork, and a space to listen to your body’s wisdom.
🌿 **Every last Thursday of the month, stay after class for a community potluck dinner!**
📍 **Location**: 727 T St. Sacramento CA 95811 ✨ **All our events are free. Donations are welcome.** 📩 **Questions? Reach out at** embody.iama@gmail.com 🔗 **Follow us on Instagram:** [@embody.iama](https://www.instagram.com/embody.iama)

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Nov 26, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: 21st National Juried Exhibition — Sun Aug 30, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: AXIS GALLERY 21st ANNUAL NATIONAL JURIED COMPETITION August 7–30, 2026 Second Saturday Reception August 8, 2026, 5–8 PM Axis Gallery presents the 21st Annual National Juried Competition, a group exhibition featuring works selected by juror Sharon Butler, founder of Two Coats of Paint. The exhibition includes works by artists from around the country in a variety of mediums. item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Sep 16, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants
